category_title: Dominant preschool children who frequently report peers' norm violations
minimal_context: The student is participating in daily classroom activities and observing peers playing with dolls in the preschool classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for free play. You can play with the dolls over here.

STUDENT: I get to hand out the dolls because I'm in charge.

TUTOR: Just make sure you are playing.

STUDENT: Teacher, you need to look at them right now.

TUTOR: What is it?

STUDENT: They’re being very loud. And they went into the wrong area of the classroom!

options.A: Acknowledge the report by saying 'Are they?' and looking at the peers, or telling the student you will talk to them without actually doing so.
options.B: Teach a replacement behavior for the student to use when observing peers playing with the dolls during the free play session.
options.C: Provide a detailed instruction of each specific element involved in the free play activity with the dolls during the session.
options.D: Use the 'bubble-blowing' technique to help the student visualize their thoughts about the peers and release them without judgment.
